propositions: An errored ItemRecord (with errored=True, decision='dropped') is incorrectly scored as a decision flip when paired against a non-errored verdict, because the flip computation at parity.py:107 does not guard against errored sides.
A single transient infrastructure error (e.g., ThrottlingException) on one arm causes criterion (b) to fail as a false model-quality regression when zero decision flips should be acceptable.
The flip gating failure string is byte-identical across arms with 0, 1, or 3 real flips when errors are mixed in, making it impossible to distinguish fabricated flips from genuine model regressions.
An errored pair with errored=True and valid=True produces a completely silent fabricated flip with no corroborating error_rate signal.
The defect violates the parity.py:46 contract (errored is not a model verdict) and double-counts the same event under both criterion (b) for verdicts and criterion (d) for errors.
